title: Caption a video
summary: Add timed words to one video using lines, karaoke_pop, quiet_captions or a subtitle track. This creates a new captioned.mp4 library asset; it does not edit the source.

carrier.notes: Operations describe the capability result before the luc_invoke identity wrapper and model-result clipping.

replaceability.why: The package carries Python code the Runtime runs, so its own files stay as they shipped. A creator's layer may add a program that answers for a capability instead: it runs only in the code sandbox, reaches the Project only through ToolHost's calls over its pipe, and is held to this contract (docs/luc/tool-programs.md).
replaceability.decided: self-Luc spec v0.3 (2026-10-18); today's code: lumeri_runtime/luc_packaged_tools.py:545-561; Acrab 2026-10-26: replaced by programs in the code sandbox

operations.name: caption_media

style.description: lines: timed lines of text. karaoke_pop and quiet_captions: one word at a time. track: a selectable subtitle stream, the picture untouched.

source.description: The asset id of one video in this Project's library.

text.description: The words. Enough on its own; timings are worked out.

cues.description: Explicit timed lines, for lines and track.

word_timings.description: Explicit timed words, for karaoke_pop and quiet_captions.

look.description: Optional overrides of the style's look.

operations.notes: No end-to-end call deadline is enforced. The first successful call returns {status: started, job_id}; replay after completion returns the stored successful result. The Runtime derives the key from turn_id, tool_call_id, engine capability and intent. Keep that context to retry; a new call is new work. The subprocess ceiling below applies per engine execution, not to the whole job or later import/notes writes. Only video sources are accepted. Burned styles use the supported software encoder; track adds a subtitle stream. Caption words and look are part of job intent. The output keeps the engine report under caption.

events.name: luc.module_fell_back
events.notes: Once per Session in a start, when a layer's program broke and the Official code answers instead.

bounds.name: agent_result_chars
bounds.unit: characters before the model result is clipped; the cut notice is appended

invariants.text: The Runtime authorizes declared Host APIs and checks the tool edit scope before a Project mutation; the package cannot expand its effective editable boundary.
A started job handle proves work was scheduled; it does not prove an asset or notes were written.
Every style requires text or its explicit timed words/cues before an engine job is created.

break: A layer's program does not start, answers late, too large or out of shape, or ends.
It asks for a host call that does not exist, with other arguments, or more than 256 of them.
Its result does not keep the output schema, or its refusal names an error code not listed here.
failure.notes: The Official code answers the same call, and every call of this Luc for the rest of the start; the Session hears luc.module_fell_back once and luc_breaker counts one break. A call whose program had already changed something is refused with E_LUC_PROGRAM_BROKE instead, and what changed stands. Without a program, a call that raises or refuses reaches the agent as a refusal.

conformance.notes: Existing tests were inspected, not run. The checker proves input equality and structural coverage, not replacement behavior or provider readiness. tests/test_luc_tool_program.py holds a replacement to this interface: the load gate, the answers the Runtime accepts, and the fallback to the Official code.

known_deviations.text: The loaded capability advertises only an object output schema. Its actual structured result below is not enforced by the current adapter.

Engine execution and its resulting asset import or annotation write are separate governed steps. There is no atomic layer patch/result record covering all steps; replay or fallback must not assume a single atomic commit.
Only the agent's call goes to a layer's program. Where the editor asks a packaged tool directly through the Worker's own routes, the Official code answers.
Stopping the turn does not stop a program mid-call; the 10 s deadline per answer and the bound of 256 host calls end it.

caption.description: Renderer report including captioned, produced and style; renderer-specific fields are preserved. Engine caption output is owned by the data area; see iface:engine.gemia/v1.

anyOf.description: Imported library asset reference, owned by the media store; see iface:media.store/v1.
